title: Congenital Cataract, Ectopia lentis and Miscellaneous

questions.q: Match congenital cataract classification per p87 table — 1) Infantile Primary Congenital 2) Developmental … A) Age at birth no progression Presentation within 1 year B) Presentation >1 year minimal loss vision wait & watch C) Severe loss vision interference foveal fixation
questions.exp: Classification Age of onset At birth no progression Presentation Within 1 year vs >1 year Symptoms Severe loss vision D/t interference foveal fixation vs minimal loss Management Surgery upon diagnosis within 12 weeks vs Wait & watch. (Book p87)

questions.q: Severe loss of vision in infantile congenital cataract is due to:
opts: Interference foveal fixation → failure fixation → sensory deprivation amblyopia without organic cause, fixation at fovea 3-4 months
Only refractive error causing mild blur, no amblyopia, fixation develops normally by 6 months age
Only congenital glaucoma causing buphthalmos, fixation unaffected, amblyopia not expected
Only retinal detachment causing field loss, foveal fixation intact, no sensory deprivation
questions.exp: Severe loss vision D/t interference with foveal fixation Foveal fixation Brain ascertains best image formed on retina at foveal point by 3-4 months Failure fixation Sensory deprivation amblyopia without organic cause. (Book p87)

questions.q: Match type with association per p87 — 1) Lamellar/Zonular m/c 2) Blue-dot m/c 3) Posterior polar … A) Autosomal dominant inheritance Congenital rubella Vitamin D deficiency B) Associated Down syndrome C) Associated Mittendorf dots remnants hyaloid/Tunica vasculosa lentis PHPV
questions.exp: Types Lamellar/Zonular m/c Autosomal dominant Congenital rubella Vitamin D deficiency; Blue-dot m/c Associated Down syndrome; Posterior polar Associated Mittendorf dots remnants hyaloid artery/Tunica vasculosa lentis PHPV persistent hyperplastic primary vitreous. (Book p87)

questions.q: Fill up: Lamellar cataract appearance shows spoke-like opacities: Riders and opacity in ___ nucleus.
questions.exp: Appearance Spoke-like opacities Riders Opacity in fetal nucleus vs Onion ring/whirled whorled appearance Posterior capsule Anterior capsule. (Book p87)

questions.q: Developmental cataract appearance per the book for posterior polar type shows:
opts: Onion ring/whirled appearance with posterior and anterior capsule labels as per diagram
Spoke-like riders with fetal nucleus opacity only, no onion ring pattern observed
Sunflower cataract with polychromatic petals in anterior capsule region
Rosette cataract with star-shaped opacity after blunt trauma to lens
questions.exp: Developmental cataract onion ring/whirled whorled appearance Posterior capsule Anterior capsule. (Book p87)

questions.q: Treatment of congenital cataract per the book includes:
opts: Lens aspiration soft + posterior capsulorhexis avoid PSCC + anterior vitrectomy avoid mixing, >2y IOL
Only topical steroids and atropine, no surgery, wait till adult age for intervention
Only YAG capsulotomy for all ages, no lens aspiration or vitrectomy required
No surgery at all, only spectacles and patching, lens left in situ lifelong
questions.exp: TREATMENT Lens aspiration (d/t soft lens) + Posterior capsulorhexis (to avoid PSCC future) + Anterior vitrectomy (to avoid mixing aqueous/vitreous) Usually >2y IOL implantation. (Book p87)

questions.q: IOL undercorrection required in congenital cataract because power increases with age, Power at Birth 2-3D → Hypermetropia: <2yrs undercorrection by ___, 2-8yr by ___.
questions.exp: IOL undercorrection required as power of lens increases with age Power at Birth 2-3D → Hypermetropia <2yrs undercorrection by 20% 2-8yr undercorrection by 10%. If done <2yr small IOL may lead to lens dislocation as size eyeball increases with age. (Book p87)

questions.q: Match CRS details per p88 note — 1) Occurrence 2) Ocular manifestations 3) Axial length at birth and ~7yr … A) 1st trimester pregnancy B) Nuclear pearly cataract m/c in CRS micro-ophthalmus salt & pepper retinopathy C) At birth 17mm ~7yr 24mm adult size
questions.exp: Note Congenital rubella syndrome Occurrence 1st trimester pregnancy Ocular manifestation Nuclear pearly cataract m/c cataract in CRS micro-ophthalmus Salt & pepper retinopathy Axial length At birth 17mm ~7yr 24mm adult size. (Book p88)

questions.q: Ectopia lentis per the book is displacement of lens, partial subluxation, complete dislocation, monocular diplopia may occur, image shows zero D, iris, golden reddish crescent, lens, inferior dislocation +16D. Most common cause is:
opts: Blunt trauma m/c d/t break in zonules
questions.exp: Causes: Blunt trauma (m/c) d/t break in zonules. (Book p88)

questions.q: All are causes of ectopia lentis per p88 EXCEPT:
opts: Ectopia lentis et pupillae congenital bilateral lens & pupil move opposite
questions.exp: Causes: Blunt trauma m/c, Familial AD, Ectopia lentis et pupillae congenital bilateral opposite directions, Aniridia, Marfan's m/c systemic association, Homocystinuria, Weill-Marchesani, Sulfite oxidase deficiency, Hyperlysinemia, Ehlers-Danlos. (Book p88)

questions.q: Match Marfan's ocular associations per p88 — 1) Ectopia lentis direction 2) Cornea 3) Retina 4) Pupil … A) Superotemporal ectopia lentis m/c systemic association B) Cornea plana & megalocornea flat & large C) Lattice degeneration + Axial myopia D/t ↑ axial length D) Dilator pupillae hypoplasia
questions.exp: Marfan's syndrome m/c systemic association Superotemporal ectopia lentis Cornea plana & megalocornea flat & large cornea Lattice degeneration retina Axial myopia D/t ↑ axial length Dilator pupillae hypoplasia. (Book p88)

questions.q: A child with tall stature, developmental delay, inferior lens subluxation inferonasal ectopia lentis, zonular disintegration due to homocysteine methionine accumulation from cysteine deficiency, cyanide nitroprusside test positive. Per the book this is:
questions.exp: Homocystinuria Deficiency cysteine → Accumulation homocysteine & methionine → Zonular disintegration → ectopia lentis Inferonasal ectopia lentis Diagnosis Cyanide nitroprusside test. (Book p88)

questions.q: Match Weill-Marchesani features per p88 — 1) Ectopia direction 2) Stature 3) Fingers … A) Forward/Anterior ectopia lentis B) Short stature C) Small stubby fingers
questions.exp: Weill-Marchesani syndrome Forward/Anterior ectopia lentis Short stature Small stubby fingers. (Book p88)

questions.q: Management of ectopia lentis per p89:
opts: Partial subluxation spectacles, clinically significant subluxation surgery refixate lens ECCE/ICCE+IOL
Only YAG laser iridotomy for all cases, no spectacles or surgical refixation needed
Only topical steroids and antiglaucoma drops, no surgical or spectacle correction
No treatment required, observation lifelong, lens will spontaneously recenter
questions.exp: Management: Partial Subluxation Spectacles Clinically significant Subluxation Surgery Refixate lens ECCE/ICCE + IOL implantation. (Book p89)

questions.q: Lenticonus is cone-shaped lens. Anterior lenticonus associated with mnemonic SAW includes:
opts: Spina Bifida, Alport syndrome SNHL + abnormal glomerular BM, Wardenburg syndrome
questions.exp: LENTICONUS Cone-shaped lens Anterior lenticonus Associated mnemonic SAW Spina Bifida Alport syndrome SNHL + abnormal glomerular BM Wardenburg syndrome. (Book p89)

questions.q: Match posterior lenticonus per p89 — Association and features — 1) Association 2) Features … A) Lowe syndrome AKA oculorenal X-linked B) Congenital cataract Congenital glaucoma Microphakia
questions.exp: Posterior lenticonus Associated Lowe syndrome AKA oculorenal syndrome X-linked inheritance Features Congenital cataract Congenital glaucoma Microphakia. (Book p89)

opts: Congenital small ↑curvature → myopia spherical → dislocation → 2° ACG Association Marfan Weill-Marchesani
Acquired defect due to trauma only, lens normal size, no myopia or glaucoma association
Cone-shaped lens only anterior lenticonus, no microspherophakia features present
Flat lens only with decreased curvature, hyperopia, no dislocation or glaucoma risk
questions.exp: MICROSPHEROPHAKIA Congenital defect Lens Small → ↑curvature → myopia Spherical → dislocation → 2° Angle-closure glaucoma Association Marfan's Weill Marchesani syndrome. (Book p89)

questions.q: All are listed as causes of ectopia lentis per p88 last lines EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Causes: Sulfite oxidase deficiency, Hyperlysinemia, Ehlers-Danlos syndrome. (Book p89)
